transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sam Park (Redwood AE), Jules Moreno (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Dan Liu (CTO, Parallax), Alyssa Chen (Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Platform), Rina Patel (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): discuss latency SLOs, p95 targets, whether hosted or dedicated fits, streaming token/sec, KV cache behavior and data residency. Next steps include benchmark run and security docs share.

[00:00] Sam Park: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, uh this is Sam from Redwood, with Jules and Priya. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Dan Liu: good thanks Sam, quick context - we run a payments risk scoring realtime pipeline, low latency is big, p95 ideally under 200ms per response for short streaming flows, and con- we have spikes that hit about 300 concurrent streams for checkout flows.
[00:30] Jules Moreno: ok that helps a lot, and when you say streaming do you mean token-by-token streaming during generation or chunked responses?
[00:40] Alyssa Chen: token-by-token, we surface fraud signals as partial tokens so front-end can act earlier. We want p95 on the full response and also tight tail for first-token latency.
[00:55] Marco Ruiz: network wise we are in GCP us-central1, we'll likely want private connectivity for PCI scope later, but initial eval can be hosted if latency works.
[01:12] Sam Park: got it. quick map - Hosted is fast to get started, predictable for devs; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for consistent throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) is the strictest for isolation. Each has different perf characteristics but our runtime aims to keep p95 consistent across them.
[01:35] Rina Patel: from security perspective we need SOC2, KMS integration and ability to enforce customer-managed keys if we go private. Also audit logs.
[01:45] Priya Desai: we can share the SOC2 pack and KMS options after call.
[01:52] Dan Liu: yeah please. also curious about token/sec numbers — how many tokens per second can you sustain at our concurrency targets?
[02:05] Jules Moreno: quick high level — on a single dedicated A100-style instance our engine does roughly 400-600 tokens/sec for 2k context LLMs in int8-ish quant, but the exact depends on model, seq length, and whether KV cache hits. For streaming short prompts it's higher because less decode work per request.
[02:30] Dan Liu: ok, our average prompt is 120 tokens input, expected 60 token output, but we do many short calls. p95 targets: first token under 80ms, full response under 200ms at 300 concurrent, does that seem feasible?
[02:50] Jules Moreno: 300 concurrent is non-trivial. If it's hosted multi-tenant you'd see variability at tail, Dedicated reserved capacity is where we can guarantee p95 SLOs. We can shape batching and pre-warm KV caches to hit your first-token numbers.
[03:10] Marco Ruiz: can you explain KV cache again? Does that work across requests from same user? our calls are stateless per checkout, so not many prefix cache hits.
[03:22] Jules Moreno: KV cache improves repeated generation for long contexts or multi-turn chat, for stateless short calls benefits are limited. But we use prefix caching for template prompts sometimes. For stateless token-by-token streaming the bottleneck is model decode latency and network RTT.
[03:45] Dan Liu: network RTT to hosted endpoint is one of our concerns - we need <20ms RTT ideally. Would Dedicated in us-central1 help reduce that?
[03:58] Sam Park: yes we can provision Dedicated capacity in the same region which reduces RTT. For Private VPC you'd have lowest network overhead but more ops.
[04:10] Alyssa Chen: what's your measurement methodology for tokens/sec? I want reproducible scripts.
[04:18] Jules Moreno: we'll provide a script - it fires synthetic prompts with your payload shape, measures first-token and full response p50/p95/p99, and reports tokens/sec achieved. We'll also run burst/steady-state phases to mimic checkout spikes.
[04:35] Dan Liu: perfect. for the p95 SLA, do you do SLOs per-route or global? We have a route for high-priority fraud check and lower-priority enrichment calls.
[04:47] Sam Park: you can set per-route SLOs; usually customers set stricter SLOs for critical routes and fallback policies for non-critical ones.
[04:55] Marco Ruiz: what about streaming vs non-streaming cost differences? streaming seems to increase concurrency but maybe same token cost?
[05:05] Priya Desai: streaming doesn't inherently increase token cost; cost is usually per-token plus base instance. But streaming affects latency patterns and client-side behavior — we can show cost models for both.
[05:18] Dan Liu: good. any caveats for quantized models and accuracy tradeoffs? we can't sacrifice accuracy for lower latency on fraud false negatives.
[05:28] Jules Moreno: absolutely - we treat quantization carefully. For fraud models you might stay at FP16 or low-loss int8 profiles; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization vs perf tradeoffs and run evals against your labeled data if you want.
[05:45] Alyssa Chen: that would be helpful - a short eval on our false negative rate vs quantization configs.
[05:52] Sam Park: noted. we'll include that as an optional follow-up.
[06:00] [00:06:00] Dan Liu: back to concurrency — do you have examples of customers hitting 200-500 concurrent streams with p95 under 200ms?
[06:10] Jules Moreno: yes, we have a payment partner that did 250 concurrent streams on Dedicated and sustained p95 ~180ms for first token on short follow-ups. Note some of our public benchmarks are in the deck I can share.
[06:26] Dan Liu: ok can you call out warm vs cold start behavior? we need to understand tail during scale-up.
[06:33] Jules Moreno: cold starts for new model instances add ~100-300ms depending on model size; Dedicated lets you keep warm pools to avoid that. We also support pre-warming policies and burst capacity.
[06:48] Rina Patel: for Private/on-prem we need to know about KMS/HSM integrations and audit log retention periods. What's configurable?
[06:58] Priya Desai: customers can integrate with their KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) for key wrapping, and for Private we can support customer-managed HSM workflows. Audit log retention is configurable via our console up to enterprise retention tiers. We'll share specifics.
[07:11] Dan Liu: great. another question - what happens when dedicated capacity is saturated? auto-fallback? queueing?
[07:20] Sam Park: you can configure routing policies: queueing with backpressure, fallback to hosted regions or smaller-model variants, or shed non-critical routes. Many customers do automatic fallback to a lower-latency but smaller model for enrichment calls.
[07:35] Marco Ruiz: how do you measure and report p95? do we get token-level traces?
[07:41] Priya Desai: Redwood Console has per-token and per-route breakdowns, plus traces. We can instrument request-level tracing with your headers for correlation.
[07:51] Alyssa Chen: ok, would like to see example Console screenshots and sample trace.
[07:57] Sam Park: we'll attach screenshots in the follow-up.
[08:02] [00:08:02] Dan Liu: about benchmarking - you mentioned token/sec varies by model and sequence length. Given our average 60 token output, 120 input, can you ballpark tokens/sec per instance for a mid-sized LLM?
[08:17] Jules Moreno: ballpark: for a mid-sized ~7B decoder-only model in int8 on an A100-equivalent, you might hit 600-900 tokens/sec when decoding shorter outputs due to pipelining. For high concurrency you parallelize across instances; your 300 concurrent calls each returning 60 tokens is more about aggregate qps than single-instance tokens/sec.
[08:40] Dan Liu: so we'd need roughly 300 * 60 tokens = 18k tokens in-flight. If one instance can do 800 tokens/sec, naive math says 23 instances sustained, but bursts and tail mean we should plan for 30-40 for headroom?
[08:58] Jules Moreno: that's reasonable — also consider batch efficiency; some workloads batch well which increases tokens/sec per GPU. But for short, low-latency streaming, batching is limited by latency SLOs. We can run benchmark to find sweet spot.
[09:18] Marco Ruiz: do you provide autoscaler to spin up more Dedicated nodes during spikes?
[09:24] Sam Park: yes Dedicated has autoscaling policies with reserved baseline + burst capacity, and you can set prioritize p95 SLOs.
[09:33] Dan Liu: what about network egress and cost? we push results back to the frontend, small payloads but lots of calls.
[09:40] Priya Desai: egress costs are typical cloud egress if on hosted; Dedicated in-region reduces cross-region egress; Private keeps traffic on your network. We'll include a cost estimate in follow-up.
[09:53] Alyssa Chen: any gotchas with streaming and websockets vs SSE? we prefer SSE in our infra.
[09:59] Jules Moreno: both supported; SSE tends to be simpler, websockets give lower overhead for bi-directional but SSE works well for token streaming. We'll share recommended client patterns.
[10:12] [00:10:12] Dan Liu: what's the instrumentation overhead for per-token tracing? does that add latency?
[10:18] Priya Desai: tracing adds minimal overhead; per-token logs can be sampled to reduce cost.
[10:24] Marco Ruiz: concerning compliance - if we go hosted initially, what contractual guarantees exist around data retention?
[10:31] Sam Park: hosted retains request logs for X days by default; enterprise retention packaged available. For payment data we often recommend Dedicated or Private so you control retention.
[10:42] Dan Liu: ok. let's get concrete on the benchmark plan and timeline.
[10:45] Jules Moreno: propose 1-week run: day 0 we get sample prompts and traffic profile, day 1-2 baseline runs, day 3-5 stress/burst scenarios, day 6 analysis and report. We'll run on Dedicated in us-central1 and optionally run identical test against hosted to compare tail.
[11:02] Alyssa Chen: can you simulate real network RTT and client behavior? our front-end is <20ms from us-central1, but some merchants are edge.
[11:12] Jules Moreno: yes, we can add client-side RTT injection in the harness.
[11:18] Dan Liu: what's the expected Redwood deliverable after the run? SLA numbers and recommended cluster size?
[11:24] Sam Park: we'll deliver a perf report with p50/p95/p99 for first-token and full response, tokens/sec, recommended Dedicated cluster sizing, and ops playbook for scaling and fallback.
[11:34] Marco Ruiz: ok great. any limitations on model choice? we need a model that's good at numeric/fractional reasoning for risk scoring.
[11:42] Jules Moreno: we have a model catalog; we'll recommend a model profile and quantization config, and can run evals on your labeled examples for accuracy tradeoffs.
[11:52] Dan Liu: if we want to go Private later, what's typical lead time? months?
[11:58] Sam Park: Private VPC deployments take longer - typically 6-8 weeks for first deploy including network, KMS integration, and airgap considerations. On-prem is longer. Dedicated is a faster middle ground.
[12:10] Rina Patel: any requirements on our side for Private regarding outbound connectivity?
[12:15] Priya Desai: we have patterns - for Private you can choose fully isolated control plane or hybrid; we'll detail networking requirements in the security pack.
[12:24] Dan Liu: ok, pricing signals — can you share ballpark cost per month for Dedicated cluster to hit our baseline?
[12:31] Sam Park: ballpark depends on instance family and reserved commit; we'll provide range in follow-up but expect Dedicated to be a mid-five-figure monthly number for sustained 30-40 GPU equivalent capacity; we'll make the benchmark run give an accurate sizing + cost estimate.
[12:48] Alyssa Chen: sounds good. one more on latency - do you have examples of p99 for first-token? we care about tail during heavy load.
[12:56] Jules Moreno: p99 will be higher — tens to hundreds of ms more depending on cold starts and noisy neighbors on hosted. Dedicated reduces p99 significantly; in our tests p99 first-token could be 300-500ms on hosted but 180-250ms on Dedicated when properly provisioned. We'll quantify during the run.
[13:19] Dan Liu: ok, I think we've covered the main technical questions. for next steps we'll send sample prompts and traffic profile.
[13:25] Sam Park: perfect. quick recap of action items?
[13:30] Priya Desai: Redwood: share SOC2/KMS docs (Priya), perf script and benchmark plan (Jules), scheduling + kickoff (Sam). Parallax: share prompt set, payloads, concurrency profile (Dan/Marco).
[13:45] Dan Liu: will do. target to have payloads and sample traffic by EOD 2026-11-05.
[13:53] Sam Park: great, we'll aim to start baseline runs by 2026-11-06.
[14:00] Alyssa Chen: thanks everyone, look forward to the benchmark.
[14:04] Sam Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite and docs.

End of transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (K V cache -> K V cash etc.) and speaker attribution might be slightly off in segments.
